div.l: And we wil be rulyd at his deuyse
In heigh and lowe and thus by on assent
We haue accordid to this Iuggement
And thervppon the wyne was fet anon
We drank and to rest went ichon
Without any lenger tareyng
At morwe when that day gan spryng
Vp rose oure host and was oure althir cokke
And gedird vs to gedir al in a flokke
And forth we ryden a litil more than a pace
Vn to the wateryng of seynt thomas
And ther oure host began his hors arest
And said herkenyth lordyngez yif yow lest
Yee wit youre forward and yt yow recorde
Yif euynsong and morwe song accorde
Let se now who shal telle the furst tale
As euyr mot I drynk wyne or ale
Who so be rebelle to my Iuggement
Shal pay for al that by the way is spent
Now drawith cutte or we ferther twynne
He that hauys the shortest shal begynne
ʆSer knyght qdquod he my mayster and my lord
Now drawe cutte for that is myn accord
Comyth neer quoth he my lady prioresse
And yee ʆser clerk lat be your shamefastnesse
Ne studyeth not lay hand to euery man
A non to drawyn euery wight began
And shortly to tellyn as yt was
Were yt by auenture or sort or case
The sooth is this the cutte fel on þe knyght
Of which ful glad was eủery wight
And telle he most his tale as was resoun̄
By forward and by composycyoun̄
As yee haue herd what nedith wurdis mo
And whan this good man saugh þat yt was so
As he that was wyse and obedient
To kepe his forward by his fre assent
He said sythen that I shal begyn the game
What welcome be thou cut on goddis name
Now lete vs ryde and herkynyth what I say
And that wurd we ryden forth oure way
And he began with right a mery chere
His tale and said on this manere

Iam qꝫue domos patrias scichite post asꝑpera gentꝭis
Premia lauʳⁱrigero laurigero ⁊ c̉et cetera .
Incipit fabula Militis . Primo Sic
Uhilom as old storyes tellyn vs
Ther was a duke that hight theseus .
Of athenes he was lord and gouernour
And in his tyme such a conquerour
Þat gretter was ther non vnder the sonne
Ful many a riche cuntre had he wonne
What with his wisdam ⁊and wᵗith his cheualry
He conqueryd al the Regne of femyny
That whilom was clepid sithea
And weddid the fayre qween ypolita
And brought her home with hym in his cuntr͗e
With mekil glory and gret solempnyte
And eke hir yonge sustyr Emelye
And thus with victory and with melodye
Late I this noble duke to athenes ryde
And al his host in armour by his syde
And yif yt ne were long for to here
I wold haue told fully the manere
How wonnyn was the Regne of femynye
By theseus and by his cheualrye
And the gret batayle for the nonys
Bitwix athenes and the amizonys
And how besegid was Ipolita
The fayre heed qween of sithea
And of the fest þat was at hir weddyng
And of the tempest at hir hom bringyng
But al that thing I mot as now forbere
I haue god wot a large feld to ere
And weyke been the oxen in my plough
The Remanent of the tale is long ynowgh
I wil not let eke non of this rout
Lat eủery felaw eke telle his tale about
And lat se now who shal the soper wynne
And ther I left I wil agayn begynne
This duke of whom I make mencyon
When he was comyn almost to þe toun̄
In al his welthe and in in al his hie hie pryde
He was war as he cast his eye on syde
Where ther knelyd almost almost in the way
A company of ladyes twenty and tway
Ich aftir othir clad in clothis blake
But such a cry and such a wo thei make
That in this world ne is creature lyuyng
That herd such an othir waymentyng
And of this cry thai wold neuyr styntyn
Til thei the reynes of his brydel hentyn
